answer: Sable, the network's scheduler, pings agents at random moments with a fresh 20-second memory-hard puzzle. It sends the same ping to every vertex in a cluster of linked agents at once. One box running fifty IDs can't solve fifty puzzles in that window, so forty-nine miss and lose the epoch's payout. Each fake needs its own 16 GB machine online all day, so rental costs grow with every added ID. If a shared box misses one signal, the whole cluster is exposed.
